title: AI Just Made Video Games Worth $0
author: xenquish

replies.author: Superb-Ad-1564
replies.body: Yep, but it’s much harder, that’s all. Did you have any successful campaigns run by AI?

replies.author: Osmosisjones37
replies.body:
I actually have. Of the seven paid ad campaigns i’ve run five were successful and they were all AI generated. Organic campaigns are a different story, but to say it’s much harder isn’t true. It’s so much faster and easier to create and test with AI. I have no experience in marketing but AI completely removed that barrier.

I can build a product page, create hero images, write a good product description, and run an ad for it all in one weekend. Before AI, it would’ve taken me over a week just to test one product, and it might not have even worked.

replies.author: xenquish
replies.body: I could see subscription models for multiplayer games pushing people away

replies.author: Scared-Tomatillo-421
replies.body:
they already do/but also WoW and jillions of other MMOs have proven the model -

supply / demand

if we can only connect to games now via third party sub services because binary exe doesn't exist(something AAA has been salivating about anyway long before this moment) then that's all that will be available- steam and other retailers themselves may become the defacto hubs for this - basically two layers (but maybe other ways to execute this i haven't thought of just now)

1. Some hybrid ownership and licensing thing. You own some files locally.
2. No game ownership. You pay a battle net subscription. you connect to battle net to play your subscribed games.

Games for profit doesn't go away at all - in fact profits probably go up for big entities that can host and scale virtual machines because now were locked into subs - this is really a hit to "software ownership" not software as a business imo
